targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted primary-source check of an audit contribution and judge disagreement; not random or expert adjudication.
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: The source attributes its winner-curse inflation to threshold-based discoveries or other selection filters, not to samples failing to capture population extremes. The audit criticism is supported at this source-attribution scope. An unselected unstandardized mean-contrast simulation illustrates one bounded counterexample, not absence of bias in every standardized estimator. Actual meta-analytic inputs/sign conventions remain unknown and the conditional reconstruction does not establish a manuscript implementation error.

targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted inspection of judge disagreement; not random or expert adjudication
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: The submitted text is conditional and hypothesis-generating. It does not assert that a specification-sensitive estimate proves substantive moderation. The criticism contains a correct methodological distinction, but treating it as an established manuscript error would overstate the evidence. A clarification may be useful; that is different from correcting an asserted conflation.

targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted source/rounded-summary check by the assessing agent; not random or expert adjudication.
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: The six experiments use bond/reward tasks rather than supplying the pro/anti-patriotic essay materials. The manuscript explicitly says the essays were taken from this paper, so identifying the actual material source/adaptations is warranted. Defeating context: page689 discusses related US-praise/criticism results attributed to Greenberg et al.; the paper can support a general tradition citation. This is a tracing/reporting issue, not proof that the manipulation or study implementation was invalid.

targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted inspection of an explicit false premise identified by a judge; not random or expert adjudication
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: The criticism says the manuscript instead describes a root sum that omits averaging. The quoted manuscript itself includes mean, defeating that specific omission premise. The wording is awkward and calculation software/formula details could still be clarified, but neither this wording nor the criticism establishes incorrect HRV computation. Keep a possible clarification separate from an alleged omitted averaging step.

targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted check of high-impact judge claims, not random or expert adjudication
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: All four reported comparison statistics are closely reproduced by the one-sample t against a .697 bound; reported one-sided p values are also compatible. This supports asking which equivalence bounds and both components were used, and why nonsignificance of a difference test establishes similar effect. A TOST component could legitimately use this statistic; these summaries alone do not prove only one test was performed or that the implementation was wrong. Original-effect sampling uncertainty and scenario-specific comparability remain separate scientific questions.

targeted_checks.selection: Post-generation targeted primary-source inspection of disputed attributions, not random or expert adjudication; no frozen judge or verifier decisions rewritten
targeted_checks.bounded_conclusion: Hauser describes principles guiding judgments without conscious access for sufficient justification, rather than the manuscript’s characterization of conscious judgments versus intuitive justifications. Clarifying operative principles versus consciously reportable justification is supported at this attribution scope. Cushman differentiates intention, contact and action principles; the action result permits conscious or post-hoc reasoning. Therefore the manuscript’s general inability-to-justify account should be qualified by principle/task. Defeaters: explicit judgment responses can themselves be consciously reported; accessible justifications do not prove judgments were generated by conscious reasoning; neither source establishes the replicated indirect-harm scenarios measure intuitive processing or justify all principles equally. This confirms a bounded literature/interpretation concern, not a new mechanism result.
